question: Prediction of progression from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI patients (Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI in both: early MCI in P-178, ADNI-1 MCI in P-185). The channel compared is structural MRI: P-185 uses MRI morphometry only; P-178's multimodal model includes hippocampal and ventricular volume, which rank among its top features, alongside cognitive scores, APOE4 and demographics. Horizon (open, last-visit diagnosis vs 3 years) and cohort differ, which the rule allows.
metric: Shared: both report accuracy and ROC-AUC. The record uses accuracy (93.6% vs 69.37%); AUC (0.96 vs 0.6951) is the prevalence-independent comparison and gives the same result.

figures.P-178: Balanced random forest, 9 features, 383 EMCI (49 converters), 75/25 random split (95 test patients), visits as units with random oversampling (Table 1: 402 test records per class). Accuracy 93.6%: Wilson with n=95 patients, centre (0.936+1.9208/95)/(1+3.8416/95)=0.919, half-width 1.96*sqrt(0.936*0.064/95+3.8416/(4*95^2))/1.040=0.051 -> 0.868-0.970. AUC 0.96, no interval: Hanley-McNeil at subject level with about 12 converters / 83 non-converters in the test patients (25% of 49 and 334): Q1=0.96/1.04=0.923, Q2=2*0.9216/1.96=0.940, SE=sqrt([0.96*0.04+11*(0.923-0.9216)+82*(0.940-0.9216)]/(12*83))=0.040 -> 0.882-1.000 (at the record level, 402/402: SE 0.007 -> 0.946-0.974).
figures.P-185: Subspace-learning biomarker from cortical thickness and volume, ADNI-1, 221 MCI (126 pMCI, 95 sMCI; conversion within 3 years), 10-fold CV repeated 20 times, linear SVM: accuracy 69.37% (Wilson n=221: 0.630-0.751), sensitivity 75.39%, specificity 61.23%, AUC 0.6951. Hanley-McNeil: Q1=0.6951/1.3049=0.533, Q2=2*0.4832/1.6951=0.570, SE=sqrt([0.6951*0.3049+125*(0.533-0.4832)+94*(0.570-0.4832)]/(126*95))=0.035 -> 0.627-0.763.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-178 reports no MRI-only model (its only reduced model, 6 features, drops the MRI volumes and APOE4 and keeps cognitive scores and demographics: accuracy 0.892, AUC 0.88 in Table 4, against 0.936 / 0.96 with the volumes and APOE4 added), no fixed 3-year horizon and no ADNI-1 late-MCI subset; P-185 reports no cognitive or clinical predictors and no early-MCI or open-horizon analysis. Nothing in either paper reproduces the other's condition, so the gap is not reconciled by the papers' own data.
performance_validity: Passes the Section 3.5 test as written: P-178's AUC is 0.96 and accuracy 0.936 (below 0.97) on 383 patients; P-185's 0.6951 is far from ceiling. P-178's design (visit-level records, random oversampling of the minority class, feature group chosen by test accuracy, internal split only) is a serious validity concern recorded below as a candidate explanation, not as the exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-178 adds cognitive scores (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE), age, race and APOE4 to two MRI volumes; P-185 uses MRI morphometry alone. P-178's model without the MRI volumes and APOE4 still reaches AUC 0.88 (accuracy 0.892), far above P-185's 0.6951. That points to the cognitive scores, but it is not an MRI-only comparison, so it does not show the explanation is sufficient.
candidate_explanations.quote: We also tested a 6-feature group, which removed the RAVLT variables as well as the biomarker data; however, this saw the worst accuracy of the three groups at 89.2%.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition and horizon: conversion by the last available visit (open horizon, mean time to conversion about 5 years) versus conversion within 3 years.
candidate_explanations.quote: From the ADNI variables, the Clinical Dementia Rating was used to make this determination based on the value of their last visit’s diagnosis.

candidate_explanations.difference: Population: early MCI enrolled in ADNI-GO/2 versus ADNI-1 MCI, with converter prevalence 12.8% versus 57% (which also makes the accuracies non-comparable, though the AUCs are not affected).
candidate_explanations.quote: Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.

candidate_explanations.difference: Unit of analysis and validation: P-178 evaluates oversampled visit records from one random split (Table 1 shows an oversampled test set of 402 per class, while its SVC's 90.0% accuracy at AUC 0.54 implies an imbalanced one, an internal inconsistency); P-185 evaluates subjects with 10-fold CV repeated 20 times.
candidate_explanations.quote: This allows for the model to be trained against 2412 exam visits (1206 per class) rather than only the 1354 from the original data set train/test split.

candidate_explanations.difference: Model selection on test performance: P-178 chose its nine-feature group by comparing accuracies across feature groups.
candidate_explanations.quote: Many different variations of ADNI features were tested for model inclusion; however, these nine features were found to provide the best overall fit.

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI with a model that includes structural MRI, and both report AUC: 0.96 (subject-level interval about 0.88-1.00) against 0.6951 (0.627-0.763), far apart on either side, with no figure in either paper under the other's condition. Neither reaches the 0.97 near-ceiling exclusion. The gap may come from P-178's cognitive-score predictors, its open horizon and early-MCI population, or its visit-level oversampled evaluation, but neither paper shows that any of these is sufficient.
